beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my second week with the Brutalist video pipeline. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Last week was six pipeline bugs, found and fixed. This week was building on top of that fix. Did it actually hold — or did the bugs just move somewhere else?

beats.narration_text: Four things happened. The fixed pipeline got reused — none of week one's six bugs came back. A brand new reel got built end to end. One new bug surfaced, in a component week one had already edited once. And both formats shipped the same day, clean.

beats.narration_text: Here's what broke. Week one widened two text labels in a portrait component to pass a type-size check. That made two boxes taller than planned. Six boxes stacked later, the last one's edge landed right on top of the footer text underneath it — a collision nobody had checked for.

shot.visual_intent: Output-only terminal card, no source shown. Three findings print in sync with narration.

"result: last box's edge overlapped the footer text" prints; all hold

out.text: cause: week-1 font fix made 2 boxes taller than planned
result: last box's edge overlapped the footer text

beats.narration_text: The fix wasn't the text this time — that was a false lead. It was the layout math. The column's bottom boundary moved up, and the footer moved down, so six stacked boxes clear it no matter how tall the text inside them gets. Verified from a real exported frame, not a preview.

beats.narration_text: Recap: the week-one fixes held, none of the six original bugs came back. One new bug surfaced, in a component week one had already edited. The first fix tried — shorter text — wasn't the real cause. The layout math was. The honest read: fixing a bug once doesn't make a component bug-proof. It just moves the next edge case further out.
